newsitem.title: DENMARK: Lack of buyers takes steam out of Danish shares.
newsitem.headline: Lack of buyers takes steam out of Danish shares.

text.p: Danish share prices failed to fulfill the promise of Tuesday's opening gains and turned back down during the day, starved of takers.
"There are no buyers in the market, it's mainly market-maker trade today," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed down 0.78 point at 127.99 after touching 128.96 during the morning. Overall bourse turnover was 870 million crowns. The KFX December future sunk 0.90 point to 128.40 with 527 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Eyes were on Sophus Berendsen, which dived 51 crowns on Monday after a profits warning.
The share clawed back some of its losses on Tuesday, climbing 19 crowns to close at 694 in turnover of 150,000 shares traded.
"The correction is completely natural. People have analysed Sophus Berendsen and done their sums. After such a fall, naturally buyers are coming foward," the dealer said.

Wednesday's focus was likely to be on SAS, which announced a sharp fall in nine-month profits after the market closed. It also announced widespread cost-cutting but failing to say by how much could leave investors dissatisfied, analysts said.
